mainTopic: Who is exempt from the sliding-scale offering, the משנה's summary of offerings by rank, and a contradiction in רבי שמעון's ברייתא about the מָשִׁיחַ
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא teaching that the sliding-scale offering (קרבן עולה ויורד) is only for someone who can become poor or rich. That leaves out the נשיא and the מָשִׁיחַ, who never become poor. רבינא asks about a king who got צרעת, and רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that he still pays from his own treasury, so he stays exempt. רבי עקיבא holds that the מָשִׁיחַ is exempt from all these offerings, and רבא learns this from the כהן גדול's own flour offering. The גמרא defends this view with ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״, which ties all three levels of the offering together. It then explains why ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ does not work the same way. A new משנה then sums up which offering the יחיד, the נשיא, the מָשִׁיחַ and the בית דין each bring for different sins. The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's ברייתא and points out that it seems to contradict itself about the מָשִׁיחַ. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Only someone who can become poor brings this offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads two פסוקים about not being able to afford the offering. It concludes that the sliding-scale offering is only for someone who can become poor or rich, which leaves out a נשיא and a מָשִׁיחַ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה says 'if his means do not reach' and also 'if his means do not suffice.' This means the offering is for a person who can become poor or rich. That leaves out a king and an anointed כהן גדול, who never become poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a source from the פסוקים for why a נשיא and a מָשִׁיחַ are exempt from the sliding-scale offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן עולה ויורד changes with a person's wealth: a rich person brings an animal, and a poor person brings birds or flour. The ברייתא reasons that this system is only for someone whose money can go up and down. A king and a כהן גדול are always rich, so they are outside this system.

keyTerms.meaning: The sliding-scale offering, which changes based on how much money a person has
The כהן גדול who was anointed with the anointing oil

phrases.english: "And if his means do not reach"
and it says: "And if his means do not suffice"
this means someone who can come to poverty and to wealth.
This leaves out a king and an anointed priest,
who never come to poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's rule that the נשיא and מָשִׁיחַ are exempt.
steps.raayaObject: The exemption of the נשיא and the מָשִׁיחַ from the sliding-scale offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: The double wording 'לא תגיע ידו' and 'לא תשיג ידו' (ויקרא 5:7, 5:11)

steps.title: Why a king never becomes poor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from a פסוק that the king has no one above him except ה׳, so he is never poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A king: as it is written, 'And he did one of all the מצוות of ה׳ his God.' This means he is someone with no one above him except ה׳ his God.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains why a נשיא counts as someone who never becomes poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו' in the פסוק about the king show that only ה׳ is above him. A person like that is above the whole nation and does not depend on anyone, so he is not someone who becomes poor.

phrases.english: A king, as it is written:
"And he did one of all the commandments of the Lord his God."

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין עַל גַּבָּיו אֶלָּא ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו.
phrases.english: This means one who has no one above him except the Lord his God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1's claim that the king never becomes poor.
steps.raayaObject: That a נשיא never comes to poverty

steps.title: Why the כהן גדול never becomes poor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from 'הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל מֵאֶחָיו' that the כהן גדול is greater than his brothers in every way, including wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: An anointed priest: as it is written, 'And the priest who is greater than his brothers.' This means he is greater than them in looks, in strength, in wisdom, and in wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains why the מָשִׁיחַ also counts as someone who never becomes poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'greater than his brothers' as covering four areas, and one of them is wealth. Because the כהן גדול must always be wealthy, he is not someone who can become poor.

phrases.english: An anointed priest, as it is written:
"And the priest who is greater than his brothers"
meaning that he is greater than his brothers
in looks, in strength, in wisdom, and in wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Does for the מָשִׁיחַ what step 2 did for the נשיא.
steps.raayaObject: That a מָשִׁיחַ never comes to poverty

steps.title: If the כהן גדול has no money, his brothers make him rich
steps.stepSummary: אחרים learn from the same פסוק that if the כהן גדול is not wealthy, the other כהנים must give him money to make him great.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: How do we know that if he has nothing, we make him great from his brothers' money? The פסוק says, 'And the priest who is greater than his brothers, on whose head the oil is poured.' This means: make him great from his brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion, אחרים, adds to the ברייתא: the wealth of the כהן גדול is something that must be arranged if he does not already have it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion read the פסוק as describing the כהן גדול as already great. אחרים read it as an instruction: 'make him great from his brothers.' On either reading he ends up wealthy, so he still never counts as poor.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name for a תנא whose opinion is quoted

steps.confusionAlert: אחרים are not saying the כהן גדול might stay poor. They are saying his brothers must make sure he becomes rich.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אֵין לוֹ
phrases.english: Others say: From where do we know that if he has nothing,
we should make him great from what belongs to his brothers?
The verse teaches: "And the priest who is greater than his brothers,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר יוּצַק עַל רֹאשׁוֹ״ – גַּדְּלֵהוּ מֵאֶחָיו.
phrases.english: on whose head the oil is poured": make him great from his brothers.
phrases.notes: They read 'מֵאֶחָיו' as 'from his brothers', meaning he's made great from their money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אֵין לוֹ גַּדְּלֵהוּ מִשֶּׁל אֶחָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק used in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the כהן גדול lacks wealth, the other כהנים must make him wealthy from their own money.

steps.title: What about a king who got צרעת?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב נחמן בר יצחק about a king who became a מצורע and cannot rule. Was he pushed out of this offering for good, so he stays exempt? Or was he only exempt while he ruled, so he must bring it now?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב נחמן בר יצחק: A king who got צרעת, what is the law? Was he pushed out of the obligation completely, so he stays exempt? Or was he only exempt while he was king, so now he is obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a question that tests the exemption of the נשיא: does it still hold once he cannot rule because of צרעת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king with צרעת cannot serve as king during his illness. If his kingship pushed him out of this offering entirely (מִידְחָא דְּחֵי), he stays exempt even now. If it only exempted him while he ruled (מִיפְטָר פְּטִיר), then now that he is not ruling he must bring it like a regular person.

keyTerms.meaning: Was he pushed out of the obligation completely, so he stays exempt?
Was he only exempted while king, so now he is obligated?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבִינָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Ravina asked Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak:
A king who became afflicted with leprosy, what is the law?
Is he pushed out, or is he simply exempt?
phrases.notes: 'Pushed out' means out of this offering for good, so he stays exempt. 'Exempt' means only while he ruled, so now he would owe it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבִינָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the king's exemption from step 1 in an unusual case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a king who has צרעת, and so cannot rule, loses his exemption from the sliding-scale offering

steps.title: He still pays from his own treasury
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers with a question: does he bring the offering from your money, or from his own treasury? He is still rich, so he stays exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does he bring it from yours, or from the treasury?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers רבינא with a short rhetorical question showing the leprous king is still exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the exemption is that the king never becomes poor. Even with צרעת he still owns his own treasury, so nothing has changed about his wealth and he remains exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: The exemption of the king depends on his wealth. A king with צרעת still has his own treasury, so he stays exempt.

phrases.english: He said to him: From yours, or from the treasury?
phrases.notes: 'Yours' means the public's money. The point is he obviously pays from his own treasury, so he's still rich.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leprous king still pays from his own treasury, so he is still rich and stays exempt.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the מָשִׁיחַ is exempt from all of them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא: the anointed כהן גדול is exempt from all the cases of the sliding-scale offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא says, an anointed priest is exempt from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with רבי עקיבא's ruling about the מָשִׁיחַ. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All of them' refers to all the cases that require a sliding-scale offering. רבי עקיבא rules that the כהן גדול brings none of them.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Akiva says:
An anointed priest is exempt from all of them.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the cases where someone brings the sliding-scale offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of the מָשִׁיחַ's exemption with רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מָשִׁיחַ is exempt from every sliding-scale offering.

steps.title: רבא gives רבי עקיבא's source
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי עקיבא learns from 'זֶה קׇרְבַּן אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו': this offering is required of the כהן גדול, and no other one like it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רבי עקיבא's reason? The פסוק says, 'This is the offering of אהרן and his sons.' This one comes as his obligation, and no other one comes as his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for the reason behind רבי עקיבא's ruling and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about the flour offering the כהן גדול brings. The word 'זֶה' ('this') is read as limiting: only this flour offering is his obligation. So he never brings another flour offering, which is the poorest level of the sliding-scale offering.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's source for the מָשִׁיחַ's exemption is the word 'זֶה': only his own special flour offering is his obligation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?
The verse says: "This is the offering of Aaron and his sons."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13. This פסוק is about the tenth of an איפה of flour that the כהן גדול offers.

phrases.english: This one comes as an obligation for him,
and no other one comes as an obligation for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי עקיבא's ruling in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's ruling that the מָשִׁיחַ is exempt from all sliding-scale offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:13, 'זה קרבן אהרן ובניו', reading 'זה' as 'only this one'

steps.title: Maybe he is only exempt from the flour offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק only excludes the כהן גדול from the poorest version (עשירית האיפה), not from the bird or animal versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe when the תורה excludes him, it only excludes him from the offering of the very poor, which is the tenth of an איפה of flour. From the poor man's offering and the rich man's offering, the תורה did not exclude him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading from Step 8. It suggests the exemption may be much narrower: only the flour offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 learned from ״זֶה קׇרְבַּן אַהֲרֹן״ that the כהן גדול has no other offering of this type. But that פסוק might only rule out the flour level, since he already brings his own flour offering. If so, a poor or rich כהן גדול would still bring birds or a sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: The very poorest, who bring the flour version of the offering
A tenth of an איפה of flour, the offering of the poorest
Poverty, where the person brings two birds
Wealth, where the person brings a sheep or goat

steps.confusionAlert: The offering has three levels: rich (an animal), poor (birds), and very poor (flour). The question is whether the כהן גדול loses all three levels or only the flour level.

phrases.english: But say: when the Merciful One excludes him,
it is from the offering of extreme poverty,
and what is that? The tenth of an איפה.
But from the offerings of poverty and of wealth
the Merciful One did not exclude him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how wide the exemption learned in Step 8 really is.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the כהן גדול is exempt from all forms of the sliding-scale offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may only exclude the flour level, leaving the bird and animal levels in place.

steps.title: All the levels go together
steps.stepSummary: From ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ the גמרא learns that whoever cannot use one level cannot use any level.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because it is written: 'And the כהן shall atone for him for his sin that he sinned, from one of these.' Whoever can get atonement with one level can get atonement with all of them. Whoever cannot get atonement with one level cannot get atonement with any of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge by quoting a פסוק. The פסוק links all the levels of the offering together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ teach that the three levels form one package. The כהן גדול cannot bring the flour level. So he cannot bring the bird or animal levels either, and the full exemption stands.

keyTerms.meaning: That should not even enter your mind

steps.whyThisMatters: This all-or-nothing rule is the key that keeps רבי עקיבא's full exemption of the כהן גדול standing.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as it is written: 'And the priest shall atone for him'

phrases.aramaic: עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״.
phrases.english: 'for his sin that he sinned, from one of these.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:13. This פסוק comes right after the flour offering.

phrases.english: One who gains atonement with one gains atonement with all of them,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאַחַת – אֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּכוּלָּן.
phrases.english: and one who does not gain atonement with one does not gain atonement with any of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New פסוק that links all levels of the offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן גדול is excluded only from the flour level.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he cannot bring the flour level, he cannot bring any level, so he is fully exempt.

steps.title: Then the king should be all-or-nothing too
steps.stepSummary: If ״מֵאַחַת״ means all-or-nothing, then ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ should mean the same thing. But רבי עקיבא holds a נשיא is liable in some cases and not in others.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, what about the פסוק 'And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these'? It should also mean that whoever can become liable in one case can become liable in all of them, and whoever cannot become liable in one case cannot become liable in any of them. Then why did we learn that רבי עקיבא says a נשיא is liable in all the cases except שמיעת קול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 10. It uses a similar phrase in the same passage to show that the all-or-nothing reading leads to a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ looks just like ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״. Read the same way, it would mean a person liable in some cases must be liable in every case. Yet רבי עקיבא says the נשיא is exempt from one case and still liable in the others.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so, then...
Hearing a call to testify under oath and falsely denying knowledge

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two phrases. ״מֵאַחַת״ in Step 10 is about the offerings. ״לְאַחַת״ here is about the cases (the sins) that make someone liable.

phrases.english: But if that is so, that which is written:
'And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these,'

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי: דְּכׇל הַמִּתְחַיֵּיב בְּאַחַת – מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּכוּלָּן,
phrases.english: so too: anyone who becomes liable in one becomes liable in all of them,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּאַחַת – אֵין מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּכוּלָּן.
phrases.english: and one who does not become liable in one does not become liable in any of them.
Why then did we learn that רבי עקיבא says:
A king is liable, except for the case of hearing the voice!
phrases.notes: This is the case of someone who hears an oath calling on him to testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of reading used in Step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same kind of reading applied to ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ contradicts רבי עקיבא's ruling about the נשיא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns only from ״מֵאַחַת״
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא answer that רבי עקיבא learns the all-or-nothing rule from ״מֵאַחַת״ only, not from ״לְאַחַת״.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: He learns from 'from one', but he does not learn from 'of one'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the challenge of Step 11. They say the two phrases are not treated the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, only ״מֵאַחַת״ carries the all-or-nothing rule. ״לְאַחַת״ teaches nothing of the kind. So the נשיא can be liable in some cases and exempt in one.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns from it, it teaches him something

phrases.english: אביי and רבא both say:
He learns from 'from one',
but he does not learn from 'of one'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both phrases teach the all-or-nothing rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ״מֵאַחַת״ teaches it, so the נשיא ruling does not clash.

steps.title: Why is ״מֵאַחַת״ different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes ״מֵאַחַת״ special enough to teach the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about 'from one', that he learns from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind Step 12. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases look alike, so treating them differently needs a reason. The גמרא wants to know what makes ״מֵאַחַת״ teach the rule.

phrases.english: And what is different about 'from one', that he learns from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 12's distinction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why only ״מֵאַחַת״ teaches the all-or-nothing rule

steps.title: It is placed right at the flour offering
steps.stepSummary: ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ is written at the end, next to the flour offering. This teaches that only someone who can bring the flour offering can bring any of the levels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תורה wrote it at the end, next to the tenth of an איפה. This teaches that whoever can become obligated in the tenth of an איפה can become obligated in all of them. If you thought a person could be obligated in one level even though he cannot be obligated in all of them, the תורה should have written this 'from one of these' with the poverty offering, or with the wealth offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13. The placement of ״מֵאַחַת״ in the Torah is what gives it its special meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ sits right after the flour offering. That placement makes the flour level the test: if a person cannot bring the flour, he cannot bring any level. Had the תורה not meant this, it could have put the phrase by the bird or the animal offering instead.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול cannot bring the flour level. ״מֵאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״, written right at the flour offering, makes all the levels depend on that one, so he is fully exempt. ״לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״ has no such meaning, which is why a נשיא can be liable in some cases and not others.

phrases.english: Because the Merciful One wrote it at the end,
next to the tenth of an איפה,

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֹל דְּמִחַיַּיב בַּעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה – מִחַיַּיב בְּכוּלָּן,
phrases.english: to say that anyone who can become obligated in the tenth of an איפה can become obligated in all of them,
for if it entered your mind that one can be obligated in one

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּכוּלָּן,
phrases.english: even though he is not obligated in all of them,
let it write this 'from one of these' by the poverty offering,
or else by the wealth offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״מֵאַחַת״ is placed next to the flour offering, which makes the flour level the test for all levels.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן גדול is fully exempt from the sliding-scale offering, while the נשיא ruling stays in place.

steps.title: The sin-offering for regular sins that carry כרת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a summary. For any sin that carries כרת when done on purpose, each type of person brings a different animal if it was done by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: For every מצוה where doing it on purpose carries כרת and doing it by accident requires a חטאת: a regular person brings a female sheep or female goat, the נשיא brings a male goat, and the כהן משיח and the בית דין each bring a bull.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which animal each type of person brings as a חטאת for an accidental sin that would carry כרת if done on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rank of the sinner decides the animal. A regular person brings a female sheep or goat, the נשיא brings a male goat, and the highest level (the כהן משיח and the בית דין) brings a bull. This is the baseline that the rest of the משנה builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: A female sheep or a female goat

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All the מצוות that are in the Torah
for whose intentional violation one is liable to karet (being cut off)
and for whose accidental violation, a sin-offering:
the individual brings a female sheep or a female goat,
and the king brings a male goat,
and the anointed priest and the court bring a bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁבְּתוֹרָה שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנָן כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that summarizes the offerings discussed so far.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For accidental כרת sins: a יחיד brings a female sheep or goat, a נשיא a male goat, and a משיח or בית דין a bull.

steps.title: The offering for accidental idol worship
steps.stepSummary: For עבודה זרה the rules change. The יחיד, the נשיא, and the משיח all bring a female goat, and the בית דין brings a bull and a goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: For accidental idol worship, the regular person, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח all bring a female goat. The בית דין brings a bull and a goat: the bull as an עולה and the goat as a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the special rules for עבודה זרה, which are different from regular sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עבודה זרה the usual differences in rank disappear. The נשיא and the משיח bring the same female goat as a regular person. Only the בית דין is different: it brings two animals, a bull as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't carry over the ranks from the previous step. For עבודה זרה the נשיא does NOT bring a male goat and the משיח does NOT bring a bull. All three bring a female goat.

phrases.english: And for idol worship:
the individual, the king, and the anointed priest bring a female goat,
and the court brings a bull and a goat:
a bull for a burnt-offering and a goat for a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exception for עבודה זרה to the general list in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For עבודה זרה, the יחיד, נשיא, and משיח all bring a female goat, and the בית דין brings a bull as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת.

steps.title: Who brings the two kinds of guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says who brings an אשם תלוי (when you are unsure if you sinned) and who brings an אשם ודאי (when you definitely owe one).
steps.simpleTranslation: For an אשם תלוי, a regular person and the נשיא must bring it, but the כהן משיח and the בית דין are exempt. For an אשם ודאי, a regular person, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח must bring it, but the בית דין is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the חטאת to the אשם, and lists who is obligated and who is exempt for each kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא is treated like a regular person for both kinds of אשם. The כהן משיח is exempt from an אשם תלוי but must bring an אשם ודאי. The בית דין never brings an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' guilt-offering, brought when you are not sure whether you sinned
A definite guilt-offering, brought for sins that certainly require one

phrases.english: A provisional guilt-offering:
phrases.notes: This is brought by someone who isn't sure whether he did a sin that carries כרת.

phrases.english: the individual and the king are liable,
and the anointed priest and the court are exempt.
A definite guilt-offering:
the individual, the king, and the anointed priest are liable,
and the court is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the summary list, moving from the חטאת to the two kinds of אשם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשם תלוי: the יחיד and נשיא are obligated, and the משיח and בית דין are exempt. אשם ודאי: the יחיד, נשיא, and משיח are obligated, and the בית דין is exempt.

steps.title: Who is liable for the three special sins
steps.stepSummary: For a false oath of testimony, a careless oath, and impurity in the מקדש, the בית דין is exempt and everyone else is liable. רבי שמעון holds that the כהן גדול is exempt for impurity in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a false oath of testimony, for a careless oath, and for entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while impure, the בית דין is exempt, and the regular person, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח are obligated. But the כהן גדול is not obligated for impurity of the מקדש and its קדשים. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists three special sins and says who must bring an offering for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית דין is again left out entirely. The other three are obligated, with one exception in רבי שמעון's view: the כהן גדול is exempt for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods. Note that this is different from רבי עקיבא (steps 7–14), who exempts the מָשִׁיחַ from every sliding-scale offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hearing the voice': a false oath denying that you know testimony
An 'utterance of the lips': an oath you then accidentally break
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure

phrases.english: For hearing of a voice,
phrases.notes: This means swearing falsely that you have no testimony. ויקרא 5:1

phrases.english: and for an utterance of the lips,
and for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods:
the court is exempt,
and the individual, the king, and the anointed priest are liable,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מָשִׁיחַ חַיָּיב
phrases.english: except that an anointed High Priest is not liable
for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods;
this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל שְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל, וְעַל בִּטּוּי שְׂפָתַיִם, וְעַל טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the three sins that require a special offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For these three sins the בית דין is exempt and the others are obligated. In רבי שמעון's view, the כהן גדול is exempt for impurity of the מקדש.

steps.title: The sliding-scale offering, and רבי אליעזר's view on the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says these sins require a קרבן עולה ויורד. רבי אליעזר disagrees and says the נשיא brings a male goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do they bring? A sliding-scale offering. רבי אליעזר says: the נשיא brings a male goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names the offering for the three special sins, and then records רבי אליעזר's disagreement about the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן עולה ויורד goes up or down depending on how much money the sinner has: an animal, birds, or a flour offering. רבי אליעזר holds that the נשיא does not use this sliding scale. Instead he brings a male goat, the same as his usual חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'rising and falling' offering whose type depends on the sinner's wealth

phrases.english: And what do they bring?
A sliding-scale offering.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
The king brings a male goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case of step 18 by naming the offering, and adds a dissenting view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three special sins require a קרבן עולה ויורד. In רבי אליעזר's view, the נשיא brings a male goat instead.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's summary: חטאת by rank (sheep or goat, male goat, bull); עבודה זרה is the exception; the two kinds of אשם each have their own list; the three special sins require a קרבן עולה ויורד; and the בית דין is exempt from both kinds of אשם and from the sliding-scale offering.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's general rule for the guilt-offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון's short rule: whatever brings an אשם תלוי for a regular person applies to the נשיא too. Whatever brings an אשם ודאי applies to the נשיא and the משיח too. The בית דין is always exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון would give a general rule. In any case where a regular person brings an אשם תלוי, the נשיא is the same as him, and the משיח and the בית דין are exempt. In any case where he brings an אשם ודאי, the נשיא and the משיח are the same as him, and the בית דין is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון sums up the אשם part of the משנה as one easy-to-remember rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule matches step 17 but gives it as a pattern: the regular person is the standard. The נשיא always follows him for both kinds of אשם, and the משיח follows him only for the אשם ודאי. The בית דין never brings an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like him, treated the same way

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה נוֹתֵן כְּלָל:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon would give a general rule:
In any case where the individual is liable to a provisional guilt-offering,
the king is just like him,
and the anointed priest and the court are exempt.
And in any case where he is liable to a definite guilt-offering,
phrases.notes: 'He' means the regular individual from the line before.

phrases.english: the king and the anointed priest are just like him,
and the court is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה נוֹתֵן כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a ברייתא that restates the אשם rules of step 17 as a general rule from רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נשיא follows the regular person for both kinds of אשם. The משיח follows him only for the אשם ודאי. The בית דין is always exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the אשם section of the משנה follows רבי שמעון's system. It also begins the ברייתא whose second half the גמרא will show seems to contradict itself about the משיח (steps 22–23).

steps.title: The ברייתא lists who is liable for the sliding-scale sins
steps.stepSummary: For שמיעת הקול, ביטוי שפתים and טומאת מקדש, the בית דין is exempt and the נשיא and משיח are liable. The exceptions are that the נשיא is exempt for שמיעת הקול and the משיח is exempt for טומאת מקדש. The general rule is that the נשיא is like an individual, and the משיח and the בית דין are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a false oath of testimony, a careless oath, and impurity in the מקדש or with its holy foods, the court is exempt and the king and the anointed priest are liable. But the king is not liable for a false oath of testimony, and the anointed priest is not liable for impurity in the מקדש. In general, for anything that brings a sliding-scale offering, the king is like a regular person, and the anointed priest and the court are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and goes through the three sins that bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, saying who is liable for each one. It ends with a short general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part gives two exceptions: the נשיא is exempt from שמיעת הקול, and the משיח is exempt from טומאת מקדש. The closing general rule puts the משיח together with the בית דין as exempt. That pairing is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'hearing the voice': a false oath where a witness swears he knows no testimony
A careless or rash oath spoken with the lips
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure
A sliding-scale offering, which changes based on how much money the person has
Literally 'like the one who goes out with it': treated the same as a regular person

steps.confusionAlert: Here נשיא means the king, and משיח means the כהן גדול who was anointed with oil.

phrases.english: Hearing of the voice, and utterance of the lips,
phrases.notes: These are two kinds of false oaths: a witness denying he knows testimony, and a careless oath.

phrases.english: and impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods —
the court is exempt,
the king and the anointed priest are liable,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין הַנָּשִׂיא חַיָּיב בִּשְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל,
phrases.english: except that the king is not liable for hearing of the voice,
and the anointed priest is not liable for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods.
Anything that brings a sliding-scale offering —
the king is like a regular person,
the anointed priest and the court are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל, וּבִטּוּי שְׂפָתַיִם, וְטוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי שמעון begun in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין is exempt from all three sliding-scale sins. The נשיא is liable except for שמיעת הקול. The משיח is liable except for טומאת מקדש. General rule: the נשיא is like an individual, and the משיח and the בית דין are exempt.

steps.title: The first part implies the משיח is liable for two sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא is difficult in itself. From the first part, we learn that the משיח is exempt only for טומאת מקדש, which means he is liable for the two oaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult. You said the anointed priest is not liable for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods. That means only for impurity of the מקדש is he exempt, but for a false oath of testimony and a careless oath he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge by drawing a close reading from the first part of the ברייתא. This is the first half of a contradiction; the other half comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא named only טומאת מקדש as the משיח's exception, we can infer that he is liable for שמיעת הקול and ביטוי שפתים. The גמרא is locking in this inference so it can set it against the end of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This itself is difficult': a source that seems to contradict itself
'It is only for this that he is exempt': it implies he is liable for everything else

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: that the anointed priest is not liable
for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods,
so it is only for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods that he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּשְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל וּבִטּוּי שְׂפָתַיִם – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: but for hearing of the voice and utterance of the lips — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the first part of the ברייתא quoted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first part of the ברייתא about the משיח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming only one exception for the משיח implies he is liable for the other two sins. This is the first side of an internal contradiction.

steps.title: The last part implies the משיח is exempt from all of them
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא pairs the משיח with the בית דין as exempt. Just as the בית דין is exempt from all three sins, the משיח should be exempt from all three. This contradicts the first part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last part: anything that brings a sliding-scale offering, the king is like a regular person, and the anointed priest and the court are exempt. It teaches 'the anointed priest and the court are exempt.' Just as the court is exempt from all of them, so too the anointed priest is exempt from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge by quoting the end of the ברייתא. The end seems to say the משיח is exempt from every sliding-scale sin, which clashes with the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the משיח together with the בית דין. Since the בית דין is exempt from all three sins, the comparison suggests the משיח is exempt from all three too. The first part said he is liable for two of them, so the ברייתא seems to contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the last part': look at how the source ends
'It teaches': pointing to the exact wording
'Just as ... so too': comparing one case to another

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא seems to say two things about the משיח. The first part says he is exempt only for טומאת מקדש. The last part, by pairing him with the בית דין, suggests he is exempt from all three sliding-scale sins.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
Anything that brings a sliding-scale offering —
the king is like a regular person,
the anointed priest and the court are exempt,
It teaches: the anointed priest and the court are exempt,
just as the court is exempt from all of them —
so too the anointed priest is exempt from all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction begun in step 22 by setting the last part of the ברייתא against the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא regarding the משיח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last part pairs the משיח with the בית דין, who is exempt from all three sins. That implies full exemption for the משיח, while the first part implies he is liable for the two oaths.
